# Studentized Breusch–Pagan test (deprecated)

<small>Source: [`R/additional_tests.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/additional_tests.R) · Help: `?performStudentizedBPTest`</small>

`performStudentizedBPTest()` is deprecated since 0.14.0: use
[`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md), which computes the same statistic. It still works
and warns, and returns what it returned before except on a fit returned by
[`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md). The model frame of that fit holds the weights of the model
`fitWLS()` refitted (none, for an unweighted model), not the estimated
weights, and before 0.15.0 `performStudentizedBPTest()` read them from
there, so it computed the statistic of the unweighted fit. Since 0.15.0 it
reads the weights of the fit, as [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md) does, and the two
agree. On a model with an offset they agree since 0.16.0: before, the refit
of the design left the offset out, and `performStudentizedBPTest()`
returned the statistic of another model.

## Usage

```r
performStudentizedBPTest(model, data = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object providing the residuals and design
    matrix for the auxiliary regression.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default.
    The response, design, weights and offset are read from the fit itself, so
    a model that transforms its variables, has an `offset()` term, or takes
    its `weights` or `offset` from a column of the data needs no `data`, and
    the model frame of `model` is accepted as `data` (since 0.16.0; before,
    such models needed `data`). Data that are given are matched to the
    observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any
    order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data
    frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the
    order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit
    dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the
    observations of the fit are refused; see [`test_results`](test_results.md).

## Value

An object of class `htest` reporting the chi-squared statistic
and p-value for the null hypothesis of constant error variance.

## Details

Computes Koenker's (1981) studentized form of the Breusch–Pagan Lagrange
multiplier statistic, \(n R^2\) from the regression of the squared
residuals on the regressors. The classical Breusch–Pagan statistic assumes
normal errors and this one does not: in the simulations of
`inst/validation/` it holds its level under \(t_5\) errors, where the
classical statistic rejects far too often.

Following Koenker (1981) and the implementation in
[lmtest::bptest()](https://rdrr.io/cran/lmtest/man/bptest.html), the procedure fits an auxiliary
regression of \(e_i^2 - \hat{\sigma}^2\) on the regressors from the
original model (including the intercept), where \(e_i\) denotes the
residuals and \(\hat{\sigma}^2 = \sum e_i^2 / n\) the mean of their
squares. With \(\hat{g}_i\) the fitted values of that regression, the
statistic \(T = n \sum \hat{g}_i^2 / \sum (e_i^2 - \hat{\sigma}^2)^2\) is
its \(n R^2\). Under homoskedasticity it is asymptotically chi-squared with
degrees of freedom equal to the number of regressors beyond the intercept,
whether or not the errors are normal. On a weighted fit \(e_i\) is the Pearson
residual \(\sqrt{w_i}\) times the raw residual and the auxiliary
regression is unweighted; see the section on weighted fits in
[`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md). This departs from `lmtest::bptest()`, which keeps the
raw residuals and weights the auxiliary regression. The residuals are those
of the refit of the design of the fit to its response, with its weights and
its offset, so on a model with an offset the statistic is that of the model
fitted to the response minus the offset, Koenker's statistic of the model
(since 0.16.0). The implementation
shares the validation
helpers used across the package to ensure that: (i) the model satisfies
minimum sample-size thresholds via [rvalidateModelInputs()](rvalidateModelInputs.md), (ii) the
response, design, weights and offset are those of the fit itself, with the
rows of `data` matched to its observations (the model context, since
0.16.0), and (iii) the
requirements registered for this test in
[rvalidateTestRequirements()](rvalidateTestRequirements.md) are met.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. A model with an offset is accepted since 0.16.0: the refit of
the design carries the offset, as [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md) accounts for it. Which model
each test accepts, and why, is set out in [`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported
models*.

## References

Koenker, R. (1981). A note on studentizing a test for heteroscedasticity.
*Journal of Econometrics, 17*(1), 107–112.
[doi:10.1016/0304-4076(81)90062-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076%2881%2990062-2)

Davidson, R., & MacKinnon, J. G. (2004). *Econometric Theory and Methods*.
Oxford University Press. Section 7.5 derives the test as \(n R^2\) from
the regression of the squared residuals on the variance regressors.

## See also

[`performBPTest()`](performBPTest.md) for the classical LM statistic, which assumes normal
errors, and [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md), which computes the same studentized
\(n R^2\) statistic on the squared residuals. The robust workflow in
[performBPTestRobust()](performBPTestRobust.md) augments the studentized statistic with bootstrap
diagnostics.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
mod <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
# Deprecated: warns, and returns the statistic of performKoenkerTest()
suppressWarnings(performStudentizedBPTest(mod, mtcars))
performKoenkerTest(mod, mtcars)
```
